title: Japan's internal affairs ministry panel begins discussing a law to force blocking of sites that publish leaked personal data
date_note: Digital Today (published 26 November, relaying IT Media of 25 November) says the panel first met on 20 November; that is the date used.
geo_basis: Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, the agency named by the source; pin at Tokyo
summary: According to Digital Today, citing Japanese outlet IT Media, Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications has started discussing a law that would require telecom providers to forcibly block access to sites that publish personal data leaked in cyberattacks. The article says an expert panel held its first meeting and that the question of communication secrecy is being examined. An interim report is planned for early 2027, it says.
plain: Japan's communications ministry has begun talks on a law to make internet providers block websites that post data stolen in hacks, according to Digital Today.
exec: A possible Japanese blocking law could affect telecom providers; the article says the legal basis is still being examined.
impact: Policy discussion only; no law has been passed, according to the article.

validation.note: One publisher read (Digital Today, relaying IT Media); the ministry's own page was not read.

review.note: date: panel first met 20 Nov per Digital Today, not publication day 26 Nov; removed time_basis; rest matches source
